intro: You're looking for a bookkeeper near you who knows QuickBooks, probably because you want someone local to set up, tidy up or run your QuickBooks Online file. Whether you're starting fresh, moving from a desktop version or just need the bank rules and VAT done properly, a nearby bookkeeper can work alongside you. Here's what to think about before you get in touch.
need_heading: What people searching for a QuickBooks bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want practical help with QuickBooks from someone they can meet or speak to easily.
needs: You've bought QuickBooks Online but the bank feed is a mess and you need someone local to set up bank rules and clean up categories.
You're moving from QuickBooks Desktop and want a bookkeeper nearby who can migrate your data and check nothing is lost.
Your VAT returns are due and you'd like a bookkeeper who can prepare and submit them through QuickBooks without errors.
You want to hand over invoicing and day-to-day entries to someone close by who can meet in person if needed.
You're not sure whether your bookkeeper should also handle year-end accounts, and you want clarity on where their work stops and an accountant's begins.
context_heading: What to understand about QuickBooks bookkeepers near you
context: QuickBooks ProAdvisor status shows that a bookkeeper has completed training with Intuit, but it isn't a sign of quality on its own. More important is whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them for anti-money-laundering purposes, either HMRC or a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows they have trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, so anyone can call themselves a bookkeeper. That's why it's worth asking directly about supervision and insurance before you share your QuickBooks data. A good bookkeeper will also be clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, especially for year-end accounts and tax advice.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you're looking for a QuickBooks bookkeeper near you and say which version you use, such as QuickBooks Online or Desktop.
Explain what you need help with, for example setting up bank rules, invoicing, VAT submissions or migrating from a desktop version.
Say whether you're starting fresh or have an existing QuickBooks file that needs tidying up.
Let us know if you already work with an accountant and where you'd like the bookkeeper's work to stop.
Give your rough location or the area you'd like the bookkeeper to cover so we can introduce you to someone nearby.
Mention any deadlines you're working towards, such as a VAT return or year-end, so the bookkeeper can plan accordingly.
questions: Are you a QuickBooks ProAdvisor, and what training have you done with QuickBooks?
Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you handle migrating from QuickBooks Desktop to QuickBooks Online?
Can you show me how you set up bank rules and clean up categories so reports are useful?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice?
How do you prefer to work with clients nearby, and can we meet in person if needed?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper who is a QuickBooks ProAdvisor?
faqs.a: ProAdvisor status shows the bookkeeper has completed training with Intuit, but it isn't essential. What matters more is that they understand your version of QuickBooks and can work with your existing file.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help me move from QuickBooks Desktop to QuickBooks Online?
faqs.a: Yes, many bookkeepers handle migrations between desktop and online versions. Ask about their experience with migrations and how they will check that your data transfers correctly.

faqs.q: Will a bookkeeper near me also handle VAT returns in QuickBooks?
faqs.a: Many bookkeepers prepare and submit VAT returns through QuickBooks, but confirm this when you speak to them. They should also explain how they keep records and meet HMRC's Making Tax Digital requirements.

faqs.q: How do I know a bookkeeper is properly supervised?
faqs.a: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Ask which body supervises them and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance.
